quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked until you stop.
Keep squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and apply it again right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and apply it again right away.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the brake pressure. Then apply the brake again with steady, controlled pressure.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The biggest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles happens at intersections.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
No, because motorcycles are usually smaller than cars.
No, mirrors are not required on motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to ride safely:
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride your motorcycle if you have consumed any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What colors should motorcycle riders wear?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green colors. These colors help other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where to find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: How should you adjust your rearview mirror?

options.text: It should show the road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
It should not show any part of your body.
It should only show the road behind, not the lane to the side.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should show the road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your rearview mirror to show the road behind and to the side of your motorcycle. It is fine if you see the edge of your arm or shoulder.

questions.question: How should you sit to properly control a motorcycle?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent and use them to steer, not to hold your body up. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you stay balanced during turns.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Stop only if there is other traffic.
Vehicles will enter the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the left part of the lane to see around vehicles ahead.
Ride close to the vehicle in front to use their headlights.
Slow down to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to avoid unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards. Also increase your distance from other vehicles and be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can make a rider cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only ride in the left portion of the lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move your position in the lane based on what the road and traffic conditions require.

questions.question: To reduce crash risk, do all of the following except:

options.text: Use your signals and brake lights to tell others your plans.
Keep enough distance between you and vehicles ahead.

questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others, signal your plans, keep a safe distance, watch ahead for hazards, and be ready to react. Dark clothing makes you less visible.

questions.question: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen:
questions.explanation: Most accidents between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to give the motorcycle the right-of-way.

questions.question: Wearing all of the following can reduce crash injuries, except:
questions.explanation: A DOT helmet protects your head and neck. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects you. A sweatshirt does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: __________ can cause motorcycle accidents.
questions.explanation: Following too closely is a major cause of motorcycle crashes. Always keep a safe distance from the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: To help others see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Weave side to side in your lane.
Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to make your motorcycle visible. Always check that your headlight works before riding.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, ride in:

options.text: The left portion of your lane.
The center portion of your lane.
The right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing driver is dangerous. Riding on the far side may encourage them to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: You face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles when riding ________.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and cars. Position yourself in your lane so other drivers can see you clearly.

questions.question: When stopped, you should stay in:
questions.explanation: Stay in first gear when stopped. This lets you quickly move away if danger appears.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, what gear should the engine be in?
questions.explanation: Put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that turns on when the key is on and the motorcycle is in neutral.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: How should you position your body on the motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should be slightly bent when you hold the handgrips.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to change to red.
The light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns you that the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, keep going through it.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should riders do?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Skip the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line and then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop line or sign, stop where the sign shows. Then edge forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you look.
